pageCache.pageTitle: Computer Science & IT - Robert May's School
pageCache.text:
Computer Science & IT
Head of Department:
Department aims:
Our students follow a learning journey that gives them access to an exciting mastery of computing concepts, embedded with diversity and ensuring inclusion. With this in mind, they learn real world topics linking to the National Curriculum in a mastery format, such as yearly escalated topics; esafety, computational thinking, digital tools, algorithms and programming.
We are living in an acutely digital age, where modern technologies and data driven identities are part of our learners’ everyday lives. Our vision is to ensure our children know that computing is an essential part of a well-rounded academic offering and prepares them to live and thrive in a world that is rapidly changing. With an understanding that computing acumen is achievable as well as fundamental in a wide range of career vocations. The overarching vision of the Computer Science Department is to transform users of technology into ethical creators of technology. Furthermore, by giving students the tools needed such as the Predict, Run, Investigate, Modify and Make (PRIMM – Sue Sentance) model to build lifelong resilience skills, working with enthusiasm independently, as well as in a team to solve a variety of real world problems.
Ethical Digital Literacy is our department’s priority, with our children developing an understanding of how to use computers safely and responsibly. With a strong sense of vocational opportunities for all learners.

Extra Curricular
“The extra curriculal programme is an outstanding feature of school provision and supports the development of character in a range of different contexts.”
ACE kitemark assessment, 2025
“Opportunities are intentionally designed to ‘tether’ students to the school by fostering a strong sense of belonging and community, an approach supported by wider research into long-term life outcomes.”
Inclusion Quality Mark, Centre of Excellence, 2025
"Opportunities to develop new interests and passions are plentiful"
After School Activities
After school activities take place every day! Students are welcome to turn up to whichever club they wish to (with the exception of those that are stated 'Invite Only' or selected groups such as Music or performance rehearsals).
Where a scheduled club is not due to run, we aim to get messages out via notices delivered during tutor time, and on social media & the website. If a club does have to be cancelled at short notice (e.g. due to staff illness), we will direct any students staying behind to other available clubs running that day.
At Robert May’s we believe that enrichment activities are vital in developing character as well as supporting emotional and mental well being. They are great opportunities to meet new friends and try new things. With over 50 activities we are confident that you will find something that suits you, with sport, exercise, music, drama and other activities available to all year groups. Being a part of Robert May’s community is key so take advantage of as many opportunities as possible (and you get achievement points for taking part which will go towards the House cup).
Extracurricular activities play a vital role in enhancing character values by providing students with opportunities to develop skills and traits outside the academic environment. Through participation in sports, arts, clubs, or volunteer work, individuals learn teamwork, leadership, discipline, and perseverance. These activities teach responsibility, time management, and the importance of commitment, as students must balance their involvement with other obligations. Engaging in diverse experiences also promotes empathy, respect for others, and a sense of community, helping students understand and appreciate different perspectives. By fostering personal growth and resilience, extracurriculars contribute to building well-rounded, morally grounded individuals.
Please see below our current timetable:
Clubs and After School Activities - Summer Term 2025/26Revision Sessions Spring/Summer 2026 For more information on Music lessons available at RMS, Please go to the Music Dept page within Curriculum>Subjects
Students that want to stay for an extra curricular club after school have the opportunity to catch a late bus on Mondays, Wednesdays & Thursdays, which leaves school at approximately 4.15pm.
Bus passes for required days of each term must be purchased in advance through the late bus pass portal.

Drama
Head of Department:
Department aims:
Taught on a half term rotation with Music, the Drama department aims to provide each student with a broad experience of the subject at key stage 3, giving students the opportunity to experience a range of different performance techniques, styles and explorative strategies whilst using a diverse selection of stimuli. All lessons will have a clear focus on teamwork, developing leadership skills and building confidence. At GCSE the Drama department aims to build upon students’ previous knowledge and go into more depth when exploring the work of specific practitioners and technical elements, as well as developing confidence in exploring and performing texts and evaluating live performance. We aim to encourage as many pupils as possible to take part in extracurricular Drama and to experience live theatre.
For more information regarding topics covered in Drama, please see the curriculum information and Learning Journey linked below

Design & Technology and Engineering
Head of Department:
Department Aim:
The Design & Engineering Department at Robert May's believes that every student should have the opportunity to learn through the experience of hands-on making. This has come to include CAD/CAM, rapid prototyping (3D printing etc.), prototyping and testing. At KS3 this year students will work in wood, metals and plastics as well as electronics. In Y8 all students will study aerodynamics and racing car design in our slightly famous F1 module.
For more information regarding topics covered in Design & Engineering, please see the curriculum information and Learning Journey linked below

Art
Head of Department:
Miss Georgie Herbert
Department aims:
The Art Department at Robert May’s believes that every student should enjoy creating and looking at Art. Through the observation and exploration of the visual, Art can open up new ways of seeing; it can develop creativity, explore values and feelings, whilst appreciating cultural diversity, enabling students to gain a greater awareness of the world they live in.
For more information regarding topics covered in Art, please see the curriculum information and Learning Journey linked below
Reading List:
There is no reading list but students are encouraged to explore the artwork of others using both the department and school libraries resources.
Students at GCSE must demonstrate an understanding of other artists and link these to their own work. This is done using books, visits to galleries and via online references.
Extracurricular and enrichment:
All GCSE courses begin with an Art trip in order to gain a wealth of resources for students to begin their first unit of work.
The department runs an after school Art club, one day per week.

English
Head of Department:
Department aims:
This department strives to provide every Upper School student at Robert May’s School with the personalised and structured support that they will need to achieve the best possible outcomes at GCSE level.
Our aim with Lower School students is to encourage a love of English in the broadest possible terms, encompassing the exploration of literature and its role in understanding humanity as well as the study of the power of language and the crafts of writing and oracy. For each student, we should build the foundation of essential skills required to succeed in further study and future employment.
For more information regarding topics covered in English, please see the curriculum information and Learning Journey linked below
Reading Lists:
There are recommended reading lists for each term of the Lower School curriculum, linked to the main enquiry question. These are published via the VLE, are available on the School Library catalogue website and are on posters in classrooms.

pageCache.text:
Parent/Carer Consultations, Reporting and Assessment
Parent/Carer Consultations
In line with the recent feedback we've received from parents, we are streamlining our Parent/Carer Consultation process. This year we have changed the process by firstly giving you the opportunity to discuss your child's Academic Progress Review with your child. This will allow you to make an informed decision as to whether or not you would like to book an appointment with your child’s subject teacher. In these virtual 5 minute appointments you can identify any areas of concern regarding your child's subject related academic progress and/or your child’s attitude to learning as well as ask for guidance as to how the child can progress further.
Please use the infographic below to help you make decisions about which teachers to book parents evening appointments with.
Click on the infographic below which includes some useful links.
The Parent/Carer Consultation events are remote via Edulink One, and are offered once per academic year for Years 7, 8, 10 and 11. They take place over three days during the week that they are calendared.
Year 9 Parent/Carer Consultation will take place over two days for Core subjects (English, Maths and Science) only. All other subjects take part in an Options Fayre, where Parents/Carers and students will be able to come into school and find out more about the specific subject areas that are available in readiness for their Year 10 to Year 11 GCSE journey.
During this academic year (2025-2026) the dates for these events are:
Consultation Event Date
12th - 14th May 2026
21st - 23rd April 2026
27th - 28th January 2026
2th - 4th December 2025
13th - 15th January 2026
How do I make a booking for these events?
All bookings can be made via the ‘Parents Evening’ section of Edulink One. Each appointment will last no longer than five minutes.
Here is a guide on how to book an appointment and a helpful video is also available to watch here, if that is easier and more convenient for you. These guides will also show you how to add a second parent/carer to the appointment, if required.
Should there be more than one appointment slot available to you for a subject, please make sure that you only book one appointment.

Head of Department:
Mr. Sam Symonds-Keates
Department aims:
Our vision is to foster a love of History and impart an understanding of the importance of the past. We aim to develop learners who are able to use their contextual knowledge to understand and make judgements about current and future issues. Students will be equipped with transferable skills, such as critical thinking, effective communication, resilience and creativity.

Year 10/11 Revision
Year 11 Revision Sessions
From the Spring term of Year 11 departments offer some or all of the following revision session options:
Bookable revision sessions (taught 30 minute revision lessons with pre published topics). These will be for groups of 10 students only. More information about these will be out shortly.
Drop in revision sessions where students can complete prep or ask specific questions about topics areas they have studied in class. These will take place after Christmas until the exams.
Breakfast revision sessions. These will be short 10 minute revision sessions which include taught material or quizzes. These will take place after Christmas until the exams.
